However, as per the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (hereinafter "FSSAI") the testing of the imported goods were not conducted as per the relevant standards.

Mr. Aditya Singla, ld. Sr. Standing Counsel for FSSAI submits that he has filed the affidavit on behalf of FSSAI along with the amended report of the NFL dated 16th January, 2025.
As per the said report the imported goods are not fit for human consumption.

4. It is also noted that on 16th January, 2025 the Court had directed the Respondents to seek instructions in respect of the application being CM APPL. 2639/2025 wherein the Petitioner has sought unconditional release of the imported goods for industrial purposes.
5. Mr. Anurag Ojha, ld. Sr. Standing Counsel for the Customs Department seeks time to file a short affidavit in this regard.
Let him do so within one week.
6. The officials of FSSAI are exempted from personal appearance.
7. List on 12th March, 2025.

5. According to the FSSAI, the testing was carried out under Regulation No. 2.12 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives)

However, the FSSAI is of the opinion that the parameters as prescribed in sub- regulation 2.3.55 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation, 2011 must be followed as the said sub- regulation governs the regulation for Arecanuts or Betelnuts or Supari.
